purpose: Records each indicator family whose closure_cell rows have been genuinely reviewed under P28A's re-opening rule (re-checked for a credible S2-S5 representation opportunity per data/legacy-secondary-source-audit-contract.json). A logged entry means a real, independent review happened -- it does not mean the indicator was promoted. Mirrors the same principle already established for P18-P26: 100% completion means 100% governed resolution (promoted, or explicitly and honestly closed with cited evidence), not 100% fabricated numbers. This file is the single source of truth scripts/p28/build-legacy-source-audit.mjs consults to distinguish 'never reviewed' from 'reviewed and reaffirmed' -- it is never used to promote a value or change a closure's status/tier, only to record that a review occurred.

entries.note: KMHFR (portal and API) and opendata.go.ke live-retested and confirmed unreachable, 8 days after the original P24 check with an identical failure signature (ruling out a transient outage); no new official geocoded facility dataset found on HDX; the Ministry's 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census report read in full confirms ward-level facility tagging exists in underlying microdata but the published report never tabulates below county. Both the facility-count numerator and the population denominator remain genuinely blocked.

KNBS's full 2019 KPHC volumes downloaded and text-inspected directly: finest published tier is sub-location, with no current-290-constituency or 1,450-ward table. Independently found and documented new context: Kenyan press reporting that KNBS compiled an internal 'Volume V' with constituency/ward population, withheld amid an IEBC/KNBS boundary dispute and never published; a 2025 Garissa High Court ruling (under appeal) invalidating the 2019 count for three counties. A WorldPop modelled (S5) fallback was considered and correctly declined: no reference figure exists anywhere in the repo to validate a from-scratch raster aggregation against, so publishing one would be an unverifiable derived number.

KNBS's full 2019 KPHC Volume II downloaded and text-extracted directly: no constituency table exists at any published tier finer than sub-location. Independently confirmed KNBS sub-counties are not the same delineation as IEBC's 290 constituencies (e.g. Kwale 5 vs 4, Meru 11 vs 9), ruling out substitution. The older KNBS constituency table is 2009-census, pre-2012-delimitation (210 constituencies), confirmed obsolete for the current 290-constituency configuration.

This is not a source-availability gap: the ten Mandera East/Lafey CAW source rows are real, official, and already correctly included in their constituency-level totals. The externally sourced ward boundary layer for this pair of constituencies conflicts with the operative IEBC configuration, so a safe deterministic one-to-one crosswalk to the ten canonical ward polygons cannot be established without risking false attribution. This is a genuine geometry/crosswalk constraint, categorically different from the other four families in this log, and has been transparently preserved (not force-matched) since it was first documented.
